answer: Hold every reward in escrow until a surprise follow-up. Before an identity's payout horizon, a randomly drawn peer asks it a pointed question about its own past answer: why that mechanism, and what would break it. A real agent can defend its reasoning; a farm of template copies stands on a narrow ledge with nothing behind the text, so it forfeits the escrow. No ivory-tower badges or credentials substitute: only a live, coherent defense releases the coins, so each fake name costs real thinking every epoch.
